item.content:encoded:
(Updated 9 December 2025)

Welcome! This page is updated periodically with new links.

Accessible Gaming talk at St. Edward’s University

On September 11, 2025, STAPLE! The Independent Media Expo presented a talk by Gary about accessible gaming. The talk addressed accessibility as a right, considerations for accessible design, and the five SPLAT! metrics for accessibility.

Here’s a link to the complete talk:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EujbbqfRsCk

2025 Appearances

Matt, Zalika, and Gary gave talks and had conversations with game designers at the following events:

April: Northeastern Game Showcase at Northeastern University (Boston, Massachusetts)
May: PAX East (Boston, Massachusetts)
August: Museum of Science – Disability Tech event (Cambridge, Massachusetts)
September: St. Edwards University (Austin, Texas)

We’re available for presentations and discussions.

2024 Appearances

Matt Shifrin (Lego for the Blind, Bricks for the Blind) and Gary Bartos (Echobatix) presented Accessible Gaming at Comicazi in Somerville, Massachusetts on Sunday 30 June 2024.

Comicazi.com

“Accessible Gaming” Google Slides

Contact Matt and/or Gary about accessible gaming:

Matt Shifrin (LinkedIn)

Bricks for the Blind

Gary Bartos (LinkedIn)

Interviews

Tech Talk with Chris Skidmore (August 2025)

Matt and Gary talked about accessible gaming with Chris Skidmore of the Tech Tips Podcast. Links to the audio recording of the interview are below.

We covered a lot of topics over an hour and a half: equitable experience in gaming; the SPLAT! metrics for accessibility; accessibility of specific games; virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR); and on and on.

The North Carolina Reading Service, a 24/7 news reading service for the blind and for people who are print impaired, has the full interview in two parts as MP3 file.

Part 1 of interview
http://www.ibiblio.org/trrs/TechTips/TECH080525.MP3

Part 2 of interview
http://www.ibiblio.org/trrs/TechTips/TECH0902225.MP3

Spotify (part 1 of 2 only as of 8 August 2025)

Websites

GameAccessibilityGuidelines.com

Game Accessibility article on Wikipedia

Color Blindness Simulator

Mobile A11y

Mobile A11y (Mobile Accessibility) is a blog for developers about improving accessibility. Bookmark the page when you want to figure out how to support dark mode on iOS, how to provide image descriptions, and so on.

Accessibility Software

Cephable

Accessibility software for Windows or Mac.

Cephable.com

RetinAid Tabletop

Card reader for many popular games.

RetinAid.net

Blog Posts

“The biggest hurdle of accessible games may be the community, not developers” by Joe Parlock (2019). Parlock is stereoblind, autistic, and lives with chronic pain.

Polygon.com post by Joe Parlock

Textbooks & Academic Papers

Tabletop Game Accessibility: Meeple Centered Design by Michael James Herron
https://www.routledge.com/Tabletop-Game-Accessibility-Meeple-Centred-Design/Heron/p/book/9781032541594

Dr. Herron is also the editor of the website Meeple Like Us.

Meeple Like Us

Think Like a UX Researcher by David Travis & Philip Hodgson

Gameplay observation can borrow practices from user experience testing.

Think Like a UX Researcher (website)

“The Human Controller: Usability and Accessibility in Video Game Interfaces” by Eitan Glinert (2008 Master’s Thesis, MIT)

Any added cost is certainly offset by an increased potential market, as an accessible game is one which impaired individuals can purchase. Furthermore, accessibility design themes tend to make games more usable for everyone, resulting in a game which will be easier to use for a broad section of the population.

Eitan Glinert
The Human Controller (thesis available at mit.edu)

Design Books

The Design of Everyday Things by Donald Norman

Norman’s bestseller is highly influential, and short! If you’re new to design thinking, make The Design of Everyday Things your first book on the subject.

The Design of Everyday Things (Wikipedia entry)

Once Norman’s book has broken your brain a little bit, pay attention to how many Norman Doors you encounter.

The Norman Door


Universal Principles of Design by Lidwell, Holden, and Butler

How does one conceive of the tradeoffs between flexibility and usability? How can design take advantage of biases of human perception? Or avoid those biases? These are the types of questions answered by this wonderful book, itself beautifully designed.

Universal Principles of Design (and related books)

The Visual Display of Quantitative Information by Edward Tufte

How can visual data be presented elegantly? How little “ink” is required to present data? People with cortical visual impairment (CVI) can be especially sensitive to visual clutter.

(Bonus points: how can Tufte’s principles by applied to design for other senses?)

The Visual Display of Quantitative Information

Cortical Visual Impairment

Design Meets Disability by Graham Pullin

If you’re going to design assistive technology, make it aesthetically pleasing.

Design Meets Disability

Pullin’s book references the carved wooden prosthetic legs of Aimee Mullins, an athlete, public speaker, and model.

Aimee Mullins: carved prosthetic legs

More recently, the Open Bionics prosthetic arms worn by Tilly Lockey continue the tradition of cool aesthetics for prosthetics.

Tilly Lockey bionic arms from Open Bionics

Synesthetic Design by Michael Haverkamp

As of late July 2024, Gary is still in the midst of reading this book on loan from the engineering library at Olin School of Engineering. Despite having only read part of the book, it’s already worthy of a recommendation.

Synesthetic Design by Haverkamp

By the way, Olin professors and students are responsible for excellent work in assistive technology and accessibility.

Olin College of Engineering

University Programs

St. Edward’s University: Video Game Development

St. Edward’s is a private university in Austin, Texas.

As a Video Game Development major, you’ll learn every phase of the process of creating games: building a concept, prototyping, narrative design, asset creation, testing and release.

Games at Northeastern

Northeastern University, located in Boston, Massachusetts, has game studies for the academic year and for the summer. Check out how many faculty members teach classes in gaming and related subjects!

Videos

Ross Minor posted a YouTube video showing how he played Plants vs Zombies using the accessibility mod PvZ-A11y available on GitHub.

Games

Wingspan Vision-Friendly Cards by Elizabeth Hargrave (Stonemaier Games)

Wingspan is the 2019 winner of the Kennerspiel des Jahres (Connoisseur-gamer Game of the Year).

Wingspan Vision-Friendly Cards

Wyrmspan by Connie Vogelman (Stonemaier Games)

Wyrmspan is a Wingspan game featuring dragons. Dragons!

The Wyrmspan cards carry over design improvements for Wingspan Vision-Friendly Cards:

Dragon Soul by Sebastian Bäverstam

Bäverstam design Dragon Soul to be friendly to people who are color blind. For example, the four castle pieces are distinguished by color and by shape.

Dragon Soul website

Now there’s a Brailled a copy of Dragon Soul!

TacTile by Friendly Bee Game Company

At the time of writing, TacTile has not yet released. However, check out the discussion thread on BoardGameGeek.com as the game designer asks for suggestions and makes design changes.

TacTile thread on BoardGameGeek.com


Mattel’s Colorblind Accessible Games

Mattel has announced it will make 80% of its most popular games colorblind accessible.

Mattel Colorblind Accessibility FAQs

Games will be rolling in throughout 2024 and will include UNO®, Dos, Blokus, Phase 10, Skip-Bo and Ker Plunk.

The Last of Us 2 / PlayStation accessibility

There are lots of accessibility features!

PlayStation.com: The Last of Us Part 2 Accessibility

Read about Accessibility Tags and other topics:

PlayStation and Accessibility (playstation.com)

Accessibility Consultants

PlayAbility Consultancy

Play-Ability is a consultancy with team members representing a broad range of disabilities: strength & dexterity, blindness, hard of hearing / Deaf, colourblindness, emotional, cognitive, low vision, and speech. Wow!

Play-Ability.net

The Play-Ability team

Easy Surf (Canada)

Check out the Easy Surf page about Game Services! The statistics on that page make clear how many gamers would benefit from improved accessibility.

“450 million gamers identify as having a disability or an impairment. …
82% of gamers think accessibility options in games are important. …
86% of gamers with disabilities connect in groups or communities related to games to share experiences and recommendations.”

Easy Surf: Game services

The Easy Surf team includes deaf advocate Rikki Poynter.

Easy Surf: Team

Colorblind Games

Brian Chandler is the owner of Colorblind Games. Chandler is also a team member of PlayAbility Consultancy.

ColorBlindGames.com

Fable

“Fable is digital accessibility, powered by people with disabilities”

Fable

Notes for Sighted Visitors

This page is designed to be accessible to people using screen readers and audio interfaces. Links are provided as buttons, or as links on separate lines.

AFB: screen readers

item.title: Echobatix 1.5 subscription with one-week free trial
item.dc:creator: Gary Bartos
item.description: Echobatix version 1.5 for real-time text accessibility is now available in the App Store. The new version improves the usability of Read mode, adds in-app…
item.content:encoded:
Echobatix version 1.5 for real-time text accessibility is now available in the App Store. The new version improves the usability of Read mode, adds in-app training, and improves support for Dark Mode. A What’s New screen appears on startup. The Training screen describes briefly how to use the app.

In Explore mode, the app reads the word at the end of your finger.

In Read mode, the app reads what you hold steady in your hand after one second.

In Find mode, enter the word or words you want to find, then move your phone left and right to search. Shake your find to stop finding.

In Barcode mode, you can read the UPC barcodes and get short descriptions for 2.8 million grocery items. No WiFi or cell connection is needed for Barcode mode.

The app is free to try for one week. Subscribe monthly or annually.

Visit the Training pages for more information:
https://www.echobatix.com/training/

item.content:encoded:
Version 1.5 of the Echobatix subscription app adds a What’s New screen and improved support for Dark Mode and iPad.

Read mode automatically reads text on an object you hold steady in your hand. In Find mode, shake your device to stop finding.

The Training screen describes how to use all four modes: Explore, Read, Find, and Barcode.

For more info about the free Echobatix Lite app and the Echobatix subscription app, visit our training pages:

https://www.echobatix.com/training/
